-- <nowiki> -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- -- This module includes a number of functions for dealing with Lua tables. -- -- @script TableTools -- @alias p -- @release stable -- @require [[mw:Extension:Scribunto/Lua_reference_manual#libraryUtil|libraryUtil]] -- @attribution [[wikipedia:Module:TableTools|Module:TableTools]] (Wikipedia) -- @see [[Wikipedia:Module:TableTools]] for a similar module. -- This module is licensed under CC-BY-SA. -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- local p = {} local libraryUtil = require('libraryUtil')
-- Define often-used variables and functions. local floor = math.floor local infinity = math.huge local checkType = libraryUtil.checkType
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------- -- Returns a new table with all parameters stored into keys 1, 2, etc. and with -- a field `n` with the total number of parameters. Note that the resulting -- table may not be a sequence. -- -- @function p.pack -- @param[opt] ... -- @return {table} -- @see <http://www.lua.org/manual/5.2/manual.html#pdf-table.pack> -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- function p.pack(...) return {n = select('#', ...), ...} end
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------- -- Returns the first `n` arguments in `...`. If `n` is negative, arguments are -- counted from the end of the table. -- -- @function p.selectFirst -- @param {number} n -- @param[opt] ... -- @see [[Lua reference manual/Standard libraries#select]] -- @see <http://lua-users.org/wiki/VarargTheSecondClassCitizen> -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- function p.selectFirst(n, ...) checkType('Module:TableTools.selectFirst', 1, n, 'number')
local function err() error('bad argument #1 to \'Module:TableTools.selectFirst\' ' .. '(index out of range)') end
local function recurse(index, next, ...) if index == 0 then return end
return next, recurse(index - 1, ...) end
n = math.modf(n)
local count = select("#", ...)
if -count > n then err() elseif -1 > n and n >= -count then return recurse(count + 1 + n, ...) elseif n == -1 then return ... elseif n == 0 then err() elseif n == 1 then return (...) elseif 1 < n and n <= count then return recurse(n, ...) elseif count < n then return ... end end
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------- -- Returns `true` if a given table is a sequence. -- -- @function p.isSequence -- @param {table} t -- @return {boolean} -- @see <http://stackoverflow.com/a/6080274> -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- function p.isSequence(t) checkType('Module:TableTools.isSequence', 1, t, 'table')
local i = 1
for _ in pairs(t) do if t[i] == nil then return false end
i = i + 1 end
return true end
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------- -- Returns the number of elements in a table, even if it is not a sequence. -- -- @function p.size -- @param {table} t -- @return {number} -- @see <http://stackoverflow.com/a/2705804> -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- function p.size(t) checkType('Module:TableTools.size', 1, t, 'table')
local i = 0
for _ in pairs(t) do i = i + 1 end
return i end
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------- -- Returns `true` if a given table contains a certain element. -- -- @function p.includes -- @param {table} t -- @param elm -- @return {boolean} -- @see <http://stackoverflow.com/q/2282444> -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- function p.includes(t, elm) checkType('Module:TableTools.includes', 1, t, 'table')
for _, v in pairs(t) do if v == elm then return true end end
return false end
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------- -- Merges the content of the second table with the content in the first one. -- -- @function p.merge -- @param {table} dest -- @param {table} source -- @return {table} -- @see <http://wiki.garrysmod.com/page/table/Merge> -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- function p.merge(dest, source) checkType('Module:TableTools.merge', 1, dest, 'table') checkType('Module:TableTools.merge', 2, source, 'table')
for k, v in pairs(source) do if type(v) == 'table' and type(dest[k]) == 'table' then -- Don't overwrite one table with another; instead merge them -- recurisvely. p.merge(dest[k], v) else dest[k] = v end end
return dest end
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ -- This function returns true if the given value is a positive integer, and false -- if not. Although it doesn't operate on tables, it is included here as it is -- useful for determining whether a given table key is in the array part or the -- hash part of a table. -- -- @function p.isPositiveInteger -- @param v -- @return {boolean} ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ function p.isPositiveInteger(v) if type(v) == 'number' and v >= 1 and floor(v) == v and v < infinity then return true else return false end end
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ -- This function returns true if the given number is a NaN value, and false -- if not. Although it doesn't operate on tables, it is included here as it is -- useful for determining whether a value can be a valid table key. Lua will -- generate an error if a NaN is used as a table key. -- -- @function p.isNan -- @param v -- @return {boolean} ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ function p.isNan(v) if type(v) == 'number' and tostring(v) == '-nan' then return true else return false end end
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ -- This returns a clone of a table. The value returned is a new table, but all -- subtables and functions are shared. Metamethods are respected, but the returned -- table will have no metatable of its own. -- -- @function p.shallowClone -- @param {table} t -- @return {table} ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ function p.shallowClone(t) local ret = {} for k, v in pairs(t) do ret[k] = v end return ret end
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ -- This removes duplicate values from an array. Non-positive-integer keys are -- ignored. The earliest value is kept, and all subsequent duplicate values are -- removed, but otherwise the array order is unchanged. -- -- @function p.removeDuplicates -- @param {table} t -- @return {table} ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ function p.removeDuplicates(t) checkType('removeDuplicates', 1, t, 'table') local isNan = p.isNan local ret, exists = {}, {} for i, v in ipairs(t) do if isNan(v) then -- NaNs can't be table keys, and they are also unique, so we don't need to check existence. ret[#ret + 1] = v else if not exists[v] then ret[#ret + 1] = v exists[v] = true end end end return ret end
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ -- This takes a table and returns an array containing the numbers of any numerical -- keys that have non-nil values, sorted in numerical order. -- -- @function p.numKeys -- @param {table} t -- @return {table} ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ function p.numKeys(t) checkType('numKeys', 1, t, 'table') local isPositiveInteger = p.isPositiveInteger local nums = {} for k, v in pairs(t) do if isPositiveInteger(k) then nums[#nums + 1] = k end end table.sort(nums) return nums end
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ -- This takes a table and returns an array containing the numbers of keys with the -- specified prefix and suffix. For example, for the table -- {a1 = 'foo', a3 = 'bar', a6 = 'baz'} and the prefix "a", affixNums will -- return {1, 3, 6}. -- -- @function p.affixNums -- @param {table} t -- @param[opt] {boolean} prefix -- @param[opt] {boolean} suffix -- @return {table} ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ function p.affixNums(t, prefix, suffix) checkType('affixNums', 1, t, 'table') checkType('affixNums', 2, prefix, 'string', true) checkType('affixNums', 3, suffix, 'string', true)
local function cleanPattern(s) -- Cleans a pattern so that the magic characters ()%.[]*+-?^$ are interpreted literally. s = s:gsub('([%(%)%%%.%[%]%*%+%-%?%^%$])', '%%%1') return s end
prefix = prefix or '' suffix = suffix or '' prefix = cleanPattern(prefix) suffix = cleanPattern(suffix) local pattern = '^' .. prefix .. '([1-9]%d*)' .. suffix .. '$'
local nums = {} for k, v in pairs(t) do if type(k) == 'string' then local num = mw.ustring.match(k, pattern) if num then nums[#nums + 1] = tonumber(num) end end end table.sort(nums) return nums end
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ -- Given a table with keys like ("foo1", "bar1", "foo2", "baz2"), returns a table -- of subtables in the format -- { [1] = {foo = 'text', bar = 'text'}, [2] = {foo = 'text', baz = 'text'} } -- Keys that don't end with an integer are stored in a subtable named "other". -- The compress option compresses the table so that it can be iterated over with -- ipairs. -- -- @function p.numData -- @param {table} t -- @param[opt] {boolean} compress -- @return {table} ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ function p.numData(t, compress) checkType('numData', 1, t, 'table') checkType('numData', 2, compress, 'boolean', true) local ret = {} for k, v in pairs(t) do local prefix, num = mw.ustring.match(tostring(k), '^([^0-9]*)([1-9][0-9]*)$') if num then num = tonumber(num) local subtable = ret[num] or {} if prefix == '' then -- Positional parameters match the blank string; put them at the start of the subtable instead. prefix = 1 end subtable[prefix] = v ret[num] = subtable else local subtable = ret.other or {} subtable[k] = v ret.other = subtable end end if compress then local other = ret.other ret = p.compressSparseArray(ret) ret.other = other end return ret end
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ -- This takes an array with one or more nil values, and removes the nil values -- while preserving the order, so that the array can be safely traversed with -- ipairs. -- -- @function p.compressSparseArray -- @param {table} t -- @return {table} ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ function p.compressSparseArray(t) checkType('compressSparseArray', 1, t, 'table') local ret = {} local nums = p.numKeys(t) for _, num in ipairs(nums) do ret[#ret + 1] = t[num] end return ret end
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ -- This is an iterator for sparse arrays. It can be used like ipairs, but can -- handle nil values. -- -- @function p.sparseIpairs -- @param {table} t -- @return {function} ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ function p.sparseIpairs(t) checkType('sparseIpairs', 1, t, 'table') local nums = p.numKeys(t) local i = 0 local lim = #nums return function () i = i + 1 if i <= lim then local key = nums[i] return key, t[key] else return nil, nil end end end
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ -- This returns the length of a table, or the first integer key n counting from -- 1 such that t[n + 1] is nil. It is similar to the operator #, but may return -- a different value when there are gaps in the array portion of the table. -- Intended to be used on data loaded with mw.loadData. For other tables, use #. -- Note: #frame.args in frame object always be set to 0, regardless of -- the number of unnamed template parameters, so use this function for -- frame.args. -- -- @function p.length -- @param {table} t -- @return {number} ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ function p.length(t) local i = 1 while t[i] ~= nil do i = i + 1 end return i - 1 end
return p

{{Stub|some formula, Rng machine page and z}} [[File:Tp_void.png|300px|class=pageimage|link=|alt=]] {{Template:Baseplate_infobox|image=File:TheVoid.png|previous_baseplate=[[Bonus Baseplate]]|next_baseplate=N/A}} {{Baseplate|Void}} is a [[location]] that can be accessed upon entering the [[Gateway]] which is located on the {{Baseplate|Bonus}}. == Void == {{Void|Void|symbol=no}} ({{Void}}) is a currency obtained by purchasing #-1 (Manifestation) which starts generating {{Void|Void|symbol=no}} at a base rate of +{{Void|1}}/s. [[File:Void1.png|200px|thumb|center]] == Yen == {{Yen|Yen|symbol=no}} ({{Yen}}) is a currency obtained by playing the [[RNG Machine]] (Unlocked with #RM (Highroll)) and activating the lever on the side. Once the lever is activated, the player will roll an [[RNG Machine#Auras|Aura]], and get {{Yen|Yen|symbol=no}} depending on the rarity of the aura rolled. == Dark Matter == {{Dark Matter|Dark Matter|symbol=no}} ({{Dark Matter}}) is a currency obtained by resetting {{Void}} progress and turning it into {{Dark Matter}}. It is unlocked by purchasing upgrade #-20 (Layer 3), which unlocks the third layer in {{Baseplate|Void}}. The '''Cube''' is a feature unlocked upon purchasing Upgrade #CB ("BFFs") for {{Credits|50k}} in the [[Main Baseplate]]. Clicking the Cube will increase its '''clicks'''. The Cube will provide '''boosts''' and '''milestones''' based on the amount of clicks it has. The boosts and milestones are displayed to the right of the Cube, in the second tab of the '''Upgrade Panel''', "BOOSTS". == Boosts == Currently, the Cube provides a '''boost''' to three statistics: Credits {{Credits}}, Data {{Data}}, and Prestige {{Prestige}}. {| class="wikitable mw-collapsible mw-collapsed" ! Index !! Requirement !! Boost !! Formula |- | #1 || 10 Clicks || Credits {{Credits}} || x(clicks / 10) ^ (0.175 + upg_13 / 500) + x0.25 |- | #2 || 100 Clicks || Data {{Data}} || x(clicks / 100) ^ (0.125 + upg_13 / 1000) + x0.125 |- | #3 || 10k Clicks + #6P || Prestige {{Prestige}} || x(clicks / 250) ^ 0.075 |} == Milestones == The Cube also unlocks one '''milestone''' as of the current version of the game. {| class="wikitable mw-collapsible mw-collapsed" ! Index !! Requirement !! Title !! Description |- | #1 || 25 Clicks || Starters || Unlocks {CRITICALS}, gain more Cube Clicks per click with a '''5%''' chance |- |} == Transformers == After buying Upgrade #CT ("TRANSFORMED") in the [[Prestige Baseplate]], the player unlocks the '''Cube Transformers''', the third and last tab of the the '''Cube Panel'''. '''Transformers''' are cosmetics the player can equip on their cube which will provide even more boosts. Each Transformer takes up a specific number of '''Transformer Slots'''. The player starts with 3 Transformer Slots, which can be increased later on. {| class="wikitable mw-collapsible mw-collapsed" style="text-align: center" ! Name !! Requirement !! Slots !! Effect !! Description |- | '''Dunce Cap''' || Complete '''Credit Deduction 5''' || 0 || ''"Gain x1.2 {{Credits}} for each empty transformer slot (up to 5 slots)"'' || '''Boost Credits {{Credits}} based on how many unused transformer slots there are'''
The Cube's helplessness can conjure up quite the hefty boost, if used correctly. |- | '''Book''' || 1M Net {{Data|Data|symbol=no}} || 1 || ''"Gain x1.5 {{Data}} on reset but get no {{Energy}} when resetting (will not affect passive gain)"'' || '''Boost Data {{Data}} at the cost of Energy {{Energy}} gain'''
The pursuit for traditional knowledge may be particularly healing; as long as you can deal with the drawbacks. |- | '''Neon Headphones''' || None || 1 || ''"Completely disable cube click automation. Time your cube clicks to get increased gain; the higher the combo, the bigger boost you get."''
After equipping this transformer, there will be a '''Note Highway''' displayed above the Cube.
The player should '''time''' the cube clicks to achieve the best '''rating''' and consequently boost their cube click gain: {| class="wikitable mw-collapsible mw-collapsed" style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto;" ! Rating !! Boost |- | Missed || x0.5 Cube Clicks |- | Ok || x2 Cube Clicks |- | Great || x5 Cube Clicks |- | Cubetastic!! || x25 Cube Clicks |- |}
If the player manages to achieve a '''combo''' higher than 25, they will also receive a buff to Credits {{Credits}}, Data {{Data}}, and Prestige {{Prestige}}: {| class="wikitable mw-collapsible mw-collapsed" style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto;" ! Currency !! Formula |- | Credits {{Credits}} || ''x(1 + (3 * min(1, log(CurrentCombo / 25) / log(4))))'' |- | Data {{Data}} || ''x(0.25 + (0.75 * min(1, log(CurrentCombo / 25) / log(4))))'' |- | Prestige {{Prestige}} || ''x(0.05 + (0.15 * min(1, log(CurrentCombo / 25) / log(4))))'' |- |} || Rhythm gaming. |- | '''Cat Ears''' || Max Upgrade #1B || 1 || ''"+25% walkspeed and jump height"'' || '''Increase everyone's mobility'''
One's pride does not have limits. |- | '''D20 Die''' || 1Qd Net {{Credits|Credits|symbol=no}} || 2 || ''"Every 20 seconds, receive a 10-second effect that can be good or bad."''
{| class="wikitable mw-collapsible mw-collapsed" style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto;" ! Roll !! Effect |- | 1 || ''Invert Credits gain''
Makes the Credits gain negative |- | 2 || ''x0.5 Credits and Data gain'' |- | 3 || ''x0.1 cube clicks gain'' |- | 4 || ''Researching and prestiging are locked'' |- | 5 || ''Audio distortion'' |- | 6 || ''Absolutely nothing!'' |- | 7 || ''Gain +15% walkspeed and jump power'' |- | 8 || ''Cube's autoclick rate is doubled'' |- | 9 || ''Automation speed is tripled'' |- | 10 || ''x2 Void gain and RNG Machine luck'' |- | 11 || ''x2 Energy gain'' |- | 12 || ''x1.5 wavelength gain boost'' |- | 13 || ''x1.5 [CRIT] boost'' |- | 14 || ''x1.5 Credits gain'' |- | 15 || ''x2 Credits gain'' |- | 16 || ''x2 Credits gain and x3 cube clicks gain'' |- | 17 || ''Cube's boosts are enhanced''
+0.05 and +0.025 to the exponents of Credits {{Credits}} and Data {{Data}}, respectively. |- | 18 || ''x7 Alpha gain'' |- | 19 || ''x2.5 Credits and Data gain'' |- | 20 || ''x3 Credits, Data and cube clicks gain and +50% mobility'' |- |} || A 20-sided die that's meant to be your saving grace or... not. |- | '''Valentine''' || 1Qd Net {{Credits|Credits|symbol=no}} || 2 || ''"Get up to x10 cube clicks gain when maximizing heartbeat; but get stunned if heartbeat is maximized, receiving x0.1 cube click gain for 5 seconds."''
After equipping this transformer, the Cube's '''heartbeat''' will be displayed above. The player should time their cube clicks in order to maintain the Cube's heartbeat at the highest BPM possible, without going past '''200BPM''', in order to achieve the highest cube clicks '''boost'''. || '''Boost cube click gain significantly with a downside.'''
With hearts come fragility |- | '''Los Cubalitos''' || Complete '''Environmentalism''' || 2 || The sum of main upgrades' upgrade levels increases cube clicks
Formula: ''x1 + log3(x) / 5, min x1'' || '''Boosts cube clicks based on the sum of main upgrades' upgrade levels'''
Three is better than one! Also awfully sounds like food! |- |}

If the player manages to achieve a '''combo''' higher than 25, they will also receive a buff to Credits {{Credits}}, Data {{Data}}, and Prestige {{Prestige}}: {| class="wikitable" style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; text-aling: left; width: 80%" ! width-Currency !! Formula |- | Credits {{Credits}} || \times \left\{1 + \left[3 \times \text{min}\left(1, \frac{ \log_{10}(\text{CurrentCombo} \div 25) }{ \log_{10}(4) }\right)\right]\right\} |- | Data {{Data}} || \times \left\{0.25 + \left[0.75 \times \text{min}\left(1, \frac{ \log_{10}(\text{CurrentCombo} \div 25) }{ \log_{10}(4) }\right)\right]\right\} |- | Prestige {{Prestige}} || \times \left\{0.05 + \left[0.15 \times \text{min}\left(1, \frac{ \log_{10}(\text{CurrentCombo} \div 25) }{ \log_{10}(4) }\right)\right]\right\} |- |} || Rhythm gaming. |- | '''Cat Ears''' || Max Upgrade #1B || 1 || ''"+25% walkspeed and jump height"'' || '''Increase everyone's mobility'''
One's pride does not have limits. |- | '''D20 Die''' || 1Qd Net {{Credits|Credits|symbol=no}} || 2 || ''"Every 20 seconds, receive a 10-second effect that can be good or bad."'' {| class="wikitable" style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; width: 80%" ! Roll !! Effect |- | 1 || ''Invert Credits gain''
Makes the Credits gain negative |- | 2 || ''x0.5 Credits and Data gain'' |- | 3 || ''x0.1 cube clicks gain'' |- | 4 || ''Researching and prestiging are locked'' |- | 5 || ''Audio distortion'' |- | 6 || ''Absolutely nothing!'' |- | 7 || ''Gain +15% walkspeed and jump power'' |- | 8 || ''Cube's autoclick rate is doubled'' |- | 9 || ''Automation speed is tripled'' |- | 10 || ''x2 Void gain and RNG Machine luck'' |- | 11 || ''x2 Energy gain'' |- | 12 || ''x1.5 wavelength gain boost'' |- | 13 || ''x1.5 [CRIT] boost'' |- | 14 || ''x1.5 Credits gain'' |- | 15 || ''x2 Credits gain'' |- | 16 || ''x2 Credits gain and x3 cube clicks gain'' |- | 17 || ''Cube's boosts are enhanced''
+0.05 and +0.025 to the exponents of Credits {{Credits}} and Data {{Data}}, respectively |- | 18 || ''x7 Alpha gain'' |- | 19 || ''x2.5 Credits and Data gain'' |- | 20 || ''x3 Credits, Data and cube clicks gain and +50% mobility'' |- |} || A 20-sided die that's meant to be your saving grace or... not. |- | '''Valentine''' || 1Qd Net {{Credits|Credits|symbol=no}} || 2 || ''"Get up to x10 cube clicks gain when maximizing heartbeat; but get stunned if heartbeat is maximized, receiving x0.1 cube click gain for 5 seconds."''
After equipping this transformer, the Cube's '''heartbeat''' will be displayed above. The player should time their cube clicks in order to maintain the Cube's heartbeat at the highest BPM possible, without going past '''200BPM''', in order to achieve the highest cube clicks '''boost'''. || '''Boost cube click gain significantly with a downside.'''
With hearts come fragility |- | '''Los Cubalitos''' || Complete '''Environmentalism''' || 2 || The '''sum''' of the main upgrades' upgrade '''levels''' increases cube clicks
Formula: \times \left(1 + \frac{\log_3(\text{levels})}{5}\right), min. 1 || '''Boosts cube clicks based on the sum of main upgrades' upgrade levels'''
Three is better than one! Also awfully sounds like food! |- |} [[Category:Features]]

Clicking the Cube will increase its '''clicks'''. The Cube will provide '''boosts''' and '''milestones''' based on the amount of clicks it has. The boosts and milestones are displayed to the right of the Cube, in the second tab of the '''Upgrade Panel''', "BOOSTS". == Boosts == Currently, the Cube provides a '''boost''' to three statistics: Credits {{Credits}}, Data {{Data}}, and Prestige {{Prestige}}. {| class="wikitable" ! Index !! Requirement !! Boost !! Formula |- | #1 || 10 Clicks || Credits {{Credits}} || \times \left[0.25 + \left(\frac{\text{clicks}}{10}\right) ^ {0.175}\right] |- | #2 || 100 Clicks || Data {{Data}} || \times \left[0.125 + \left(\frac{\text{clicks}}{100}\right) ^ {0.125}\right] |- | #3 || 10k Clicks + #6P || Prestige {{Prestige}} || \times \left[0.075 + \left(\frac{\text{clicks}}{250}\right) ^ {0.075}\right] |} == Milestones == The Cube also unlocks one '''milestone''' as of the current version of the game. {| class="wikitable" ! Index !! Requirement !! Title !! '''Transformers''' are cosmetics the player can equip on their cube which will provide even more boosts. Each Transformer takes up a specific number of '''Transformer Slots'''. The player starts with 3 Transformer Slots, which can be increased later on. {| class="wikitable" style="text-align: center" ! Name !! Requirement !! Slots !! Effect !! The pursuit for traditional knowledge may be particularly healing; as long as you can deal with the drawbacks. |- | '''Neon Headphones''' || None || 1 || ''"Completely disable cube click automation. Time your cube clicks to get increased gain; the higher the combo, the bigger boost you get."''

== Features == === Chest === [[File:Chest.png|200px|thumb|right]] :''Main article: [[Chest]]'' The Chest is unlocked upon purchasing #1fh (Harvest) and is used to view your fishing inventory, equip fishing tools, sell fish, and more. === Market === [[File:Market.png|200px|thumb|right]] :''Main article: [[Market]]'' The Market grants the ability to buy items at the market is unlocked upon purchasing #2fh (Gear up) and is used to exchange {{Fish|Fish|symbol=no}} for Fishing Tools and Fishing Baits. === Enchanting === [[File:Enchanting.png|200px|thumb|right]] :''Main article: [[Enchanting]]'' Enchanting is unlocked upon purchasing #3fh (Sparkle up) and is used to enchant Fishing Rods with {{Fish|Fish|symbol=no}} which gives them special boosts === Entries === [[File:Entries.png|200px|thumb|right]] :''Main article: [[Entries]]'' Entries are unlocked upon purchasing #4fh (Look up) === Upgrades === [[File:Upgrades.png|200px|thumb|right]] :''Main article: [[Upgrades]]'' Upgrades is unlocked upon purchasing #5fh (Grade up... what?) and is used to purchase fishing stat boosts and other perks using Fish items and {{Fish|Fish|symbol=no}}. === Fishing Spot === [[File:Fishing_spot.png|200px|thumb|right]] :''Main article: [[Fishing Spot]]'' you fish in these === Cube Teleporter === [[File:CubeTeleporter.png|200px|thumb|right]] :''Main article: [[Cube Teleporter]] The {{Credits|Cube teleporter|symbol=no}} is a feature unlocked by multiple upgrades. It allows the player to teleport to different zones of the game. This baseplates's Cube Teleporter teleport the player to the [[Bonus Baseplate]] == Characters == === Mermaid === [[File:Mermaid.png|200px|thumb|right]] :''Main article: [[Mermaid]]'' Mermaid (also known as Fish) is the personification of the {{Fish|Fish|symbol=no}} currency. She serves as the tutorial for fishing since when you talk to her she teaches you how to equip rods, cast the player's rod, play the fishing minigame, and sell fish. === Aitplayz === [[File:Aitplayz.png|200px|thumb|right]] :''Main article: [[Aitplayz]]'' Aitplayz (also known as Aitplay_z) is Aitplay_z's self insert. [[Category:Locations]]

== Features == === Chest === [[File:Chest.png|200px|thumb|right]] :''Main article: [[Chest]]'' The Chest is unlocked upon purchasing #1fh (Harvest) and is used to view your fishing inventory, equip fishing tools, sell fish, and more. === Market === [[File:Market.png|200px|thumb|right]] :''Main article: [[Market]]'' The Market grants the ability to buy items at the market is unlocked upon purchasing #2fh (Gear up) and is used to exchange {{Fish|Fish|symbol=no}} for Fishing Tools and Fishing Baits. === Enchanting === [[File:Enchanting.png|200px|thumb|right]] :''Main article: [[Enchanting]]'' Enchanting is unlocked upon purchasing #3fh (Sparkle up) and is used to enchant Fishing Rods with {{Fish|Fish|symbol=no}} which gives them special boosts === Entries === [[File:Entries.png|200px|thumb|right]] :''Main article: [[Entries]]'' Entries are unlocked upon purchasing #4fh (Look up) === Upgrades === [[File:Upgrades.png|200px|thumb|right]] :''Main article: [[Upgrades]]'' Upgrades is unlocked upon purchasing #5fh (Grade up... what?) and is used to purchase fishing stat boosts and other perks using Fish items and {{Fish|Fish|symbol=no}}. === Fishing Spot === [[File:Fishing_spot.png|200px|thumb|right]] :''Main article: [[Fishing Spot]]'' you fish in these === Cube Teleporter === [[File:CubeTeleporter.png|200px|thumb|right]] :''Main article: [[Cube Teleporter]] The {{Credits|Cube teleporter|symbol=no}} is a feature unlocked by multiple upgrades. It allows the player to teleport to different zones of the game. This baseplates's Cube Teleporter teleport the player to the [[Bonus Baseplate]] == Characters == === Mermaid === [[File:Mermaid.png|200px|thumb|right]] :''Main article: [[Mermaid]]'' Mermaid (also known as Fish) is the personification of the {{Fish|Fish|symbol=no}} currency. She serves as the tutorial for fishing since when you talk to her she teaches you how to equip rods, cast the player's rod, play the fishing minigame, and sell fish. === Aitplayz === [[File:Aitplayz.png|200px|thumb|right]] :''Main article: [[Aitplayz]]'' Aitplayz (also known as Aitplay_z) is Aitplay_z's self insert. '''Upgrade Tags''' are a feature that's used to classify different upgrades depending on the effect they have, where they are and more. {| class="wikitable" ! Upgrade Tag !! Description |- | rowspan="2" | Color Tags
|- | {{Tag|Upgrade|Blue}} || Usually the unlock of a new area or a large amount of progression. |- | {{Tag|Upgrade|Green}} || Usually associated with addition. |- | {{Tag|Upgrade|Orange}} || Usually associated with multiplication. |- | {{Tag|Upgrade|Red}} || Usually associated with the modification of other upgrades. |- | {{Tag|Upgrade|Purple}} || Usually associated with mechanics and exponentiation. |- | {{Tag|Upgrade|Purple}} || Usually associated with mechanics and exponentiation. |- | {{Tag|Upgrade|Cyan}} || Affects other [CYAN] upgrades. |- | {{Tag|Upgrade|Greenq}} || The modified version of certain upgrades inside Environmentalism. |- | rowspan="2" | Other Tags |}

Associated with more complicated boosts rather than static ones. |- | {{Tag|Upgrade|C-side}} || Donation Baseplate's prefix for -c$. Associated with unlocks. |- | {{Tag|Upgrade|Greenq}} || The modified version of certain upgrades inside Environmentalism. |- | {{Tag|Upgrade|Message}} || ??? |- | {{Tag|Upgrade|Risky}} || Upgrades that (may) have a downside to them. |- |}

There are 5 badges in the game as of v1.0. those being, RESEARCH, PRESTIGE, HOMEFINDER, BETA TESTER, and [*] UNREALITY
== Badges == === RESEARCH === RESEARCH is the first badge listed, it is also the easiest by far, having an obtainment rate of 80%. It can be obtained by doing a research reset at the RESEARCH button for at least 500 Credits.
=== PRESTIGE === PRESTIGE is the second badge listed. It can be obtained by prestiging at the PRESTIGE button for at least 1 trillion Credits. This badge used to be the RESEARCH badge during the beta testing period but was changed to what we have now a bit after it ended. so if you did a research reset during the beta test period and never prestiged during v1.0 and later, you can have this badge without ever prestiging.
=== HOMEFINDER === HOMEFINDER is the third badge listed. It is currently the only badge you can obtain from a challenge at the Pyramid. This badge can be obtained by completing the Homefinder challenge at the Pyramid in the Prestige Baseplate. A guide will be made at a later date possibly.
=== BETA TESTER === BETA TESTER is the fourth badge listed. along with UNREALITY, it is '''impossible to obtain''' as of now since it was only obtainable during a 2 day beta test. During the beta test period, it was originally the RESEARCH badge but it was changed to what we have now a little bit after the beta test ended. so that means that not everyone who joined during the beta test period got the badge.
=== [*] UNREALITY === [*] UNREALITY, or commonly known as UNREALITY, is the fifth badge listed. along with BETA TESTER, it is '''impossible to obtain''' as of now, but it will be '''obtainable in the future'''. UNREALITY is very different from all of the other badges since it is a very difficult puzzle with multiple steps, but only step 1 of the puzzle is in the game currently. '''A guide page will be made''' once a handful of people obtain this badge.

revision.text: == Summary == research badge
== Summary == homefinder badge
== Summary == Sprite for the Red Wavelength

The '''Core''' is a feature unlocked alongside the {{Energy|Energy|symbol=no}} {{Energy}} currency after the player purchases Upgrade #CR ("Electric hum") in the [[Research Baseplate]] at the price of {{Data|25}}. Following the Core's unlocking, the player will start gaining the same amount of {{Energy|Energy|symbol=no}} as {{Data|Data|symbol=no}} upon performing a RESEARCH reset. {{Energy|Energy|symbol=no}} is necessary for unlocking the three currently available '''Wavelengths''' and, later on, for purchasing '''Upgrades'''. == Wavelengths == '''Wavelengths''' are available at the core as long as the player has the amount of {{Energy}} necessary to unlock them. The player has the option to '''focus''' on the desired Wavelength, which will start generating the respective {{Wavelength|white|Wavelength Energy|symbol=no}} {{Wavelength|white}}. Each Wavelength has different '''Milestones''' that will end up providing many useful boosts. {| class="wikitable mw-collapsible mw-collapsed" style="text-align: center; width: 90vw;" ! style="width: 15%" | Gem ! style="width: 5%" | Wavelength ! style="width: 5%" | Requirement ! style="width: 75%" | Milestones |- | [[File:Red Wavelength.png|200px]] || Red || {{Energy|10}} || {| class="wikitable mw-collapsible mw-collapsed" style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; text-align: center; width: 95%;" ! style="width: 25%" | Name ! style="width: 25%" | Requirement ! style="width: 50%" | Effect |- | Addition R || {{Wavelength|red|10}} || Gain +20/s {{Credits}} for every order of magnitude of {{Wavelength|red|Red Wavelength}} attained
(eg: 1 → 1 OoM → +20/s, 10 → 2 OoMs → +40/s, ...) |- | Cap R || {{Wavelength|red|1k}} || Upgrade #3's cap gets increased by {{Wavelength|red|+20|symbol=no}} |- | Buff R || {{Wavelength|red|5k}} || Upgrade #10's gain gets increased by {{Wavelength|red|+2/s2|symbol=no}} |- | Welfare+ || {{Wavelength|red|25k}} || Upgrade #6R's condition gets increased by {{Wavelength|red|x5k|symbol=no}} |} |- | [[File:Orange Wavelength.png|200px]] || Orange || {{Energy|1k}} || {| class="wikitable mw-collapsible mw-collapsed" style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; text-align: center; width: 95%;" ! style="width: 25%" | Name ! style="width: 25%" | Requirement ! style="width: 50%" | Effect |- | Credits O || {{Wavelength|orange|1k}} || Gain +0.1x {{Credits}} for every order of magnitude of {{Wavelength|orange|Orange Wavelength}} attained
(eg: 1 → 1 OoM → x1.1, 10 → 2 OoMs → x1.2, ...) |- | Data O || {{Wavelength|orange|10k}} || Gain +0.05x {{Data}} for every order of magnitude of {{Wavelength|orange|Orange Wavelength}} attained

This page details information and history about all updates and versions alike released within Upgradex, from the events leading up to it and what happened after and inbetween.
In this page, an update means a major change to the game, adding a lot of features while a change, patch or hotfix are smaller updates that help improve the game in other ways.

All individual changes are listed at the bottom of each version, and all specific times are in UTC+7 (for now).

Beta Test= From the 26th to the 28th of May 2026, Upgradex was accessible for 50 hours to players as public testing, known as the Beta Test, allowing players to have their first look at the game, albeit unfinished and unbalanced around this time. The following gameplay were included in this version: :* Main content had 3 Baseplates (specifically {{Baseplate|Main}}, {{Baseplate|Research}}, {{Baseplate|Prestige}}), with progression from upgrade {{Upgrade|Credits|#1 (New shore)}} up until the completion of [[Pyramid#Challenges|Homefinder]]. :* Optional content included 2 Baseplates (namely {{Baseplate|Bonus}} and {{Baseplate|Donation}}), wherein {{Baseplate|Bonus}} had self-inserts from the Developers and Staff Team, an extension with [[Fish Island]] relating to {{Baseplate|Bonus}} progression, and access to [[Gateway|The Gateway]], leading to {{Baseplate|Void}} which is another section of optional content. On the other hand, {{Baseplate|Donation}} was focused around Robux donations from the player, however players who couldn't donate can still progress, albeit much slower than through donating. === Pre-Release === [[File:Betaplaytestnotice.png|550px|thumb|The image posted by Lead Developer ''a_sapian'' about information relating to the Beta Test, rewards and notices]] For this period of the game, to help speed up development progress and incentivize playing, rewards were available for playing the game and reporting bugs to the developers. While not mentioned, there was also an exclusive in-game badge to those who performed a {{Data|Research Reset|symbol=no}} during the time period, known as [[Badges|BETA TESTER]].
At 13:00 May 26th, 2026, Upgradex was open to the public for the first time since development.
=== Post-Release === A few hours later, reward (b), as seen in the image contained within the section above, was then extended to be given to the top 3 best performing players instead, due to an unexpectedly high amount of CCU (Concurrent Users) seen within the game during the first hour.
With around 31 hours left during the Beta Test, Lead Developer ''a_sapian'' posted an update to current rankings relating to current points obtained through various means: [[File:Betatesthalftime.png|550px|thumb|center|Half-time statistics of the Beta Test]] Once the Beta Test concluded, a score conversion table was disclosed to the playerbase, where depending on your leaderboard placement in a currency, you would gain the respective amount of points in return, then summed up through all leaderboard catagories (except {{Data|Research Resets|symbol=no}} and {{Prestige|Prestige Resets|symbol=no}}). Then, the final statistics for the top 17 best performing players (servers) were announced: [[File:Betateststats.jpeg|550px|thumb|Final statistics posted by ''a_sapian'']] {| class="wikitable"; style="text-align:center" ! Leaderboard Placement ! Points Gained |- | 1st Place | +100pts |- | 2nd Place | +60pts |- | 3rd Place | +40pts |- | 4th Place | +25pts |- | 5th Place | +18pts |- | 6th Place | +14pts |- | 7th Place | +11pts |- | 8th Place | +8pts |- | 9th Place | +6pts |- | 10th Place | +5pts |}
In the image to the right: :*The top 3 (highlighted in '''bold''') received the Lunatic role. :*Around 21 of the top players who performed the best during this period were given the Beta Playtester+ role, instead of the normal Beta Playtester role. :* The rest of the players who had atleast 1 point were given the Beta Playtester role. However, the top player ''freakhandshake'' voluntarily gave up their Lunatic role to give to the 4th place ''mite3141'' as ''freakhandshake'' was a shared account among top players, and thus would be unethical play.
=== Update Log === While the Beta Test was ongoing, a few hotfixes and changes were released once the reports started to pour in, allowing players to have a smoother experience with the game:

|-| Update v1.0 / Official Release= Update v1.0, also known as the official release was the first update in Upgradex, releasing alongside the game on the 5th of July, 2026. The gameplay and content featured in this version was mostly the same compared to the Beta Test version, with balancing changes and some minor additions for a smoother experience.
=== Pre-Release === 4 days before the game's release (July 1st, 2026), Lead Developer ''a_sapian'' posted an image of the number 4 with the background being taken in-game, hinting at a countdown to the initial release. Subsequent updates for the countdown were then posted when it reached 3 and 2 days, then 6 hours left respectively, with the image for the countdown being 2 days left and 6 hours left fully revealing the countdown, now reading ''"2 days left"'' and ''"6 hours left"'', extra details added with the Orthogon Studios icon in the bottom-right corner and currencies floating above. File:4countdown.png|thumb|300px|Countdown at 4 days left before release File:3countdown.png|thumb|300px|Countdown at 3 days left before release File:2countdown.png|thumb|300px|Countdown at 2 days left before release, now with extra details and the full countdown revealed File:6hourscountdown.png|thumb|300px|Countdown at 6 hours left before release, with the same details as the previous image https://youtu.be/ZaywM8mSfMo On the 4th of July, just a day before release, Developer ''TerribleAtCreating ([[Paper Dimension#terriac|terriac]])'' announced that, with the game's release, there would also be an optional badge for players to obtain, that being [[Secrets#UNREALITY|UNREALITY]], a very difficult puzzle that when solved, would reward the player the badge and the Lunatic role in the Discord server. However, this badge was to only be partially released in Update v1.0, and would only be continued with enough engagement from the community.

On the same day, Lead Developer ''a_sapian'' announced both the game's release date, being on the 5th of July, 2026 at 20:00 and uploaded Upgradex's Release Trailer, which can be watched below:

Around this time, some questions were answered relating to an All Ages release and in-game changes, which were answered below: #Data will not be carried over from the Beta Test (aka. your save files will be reset), as multiple balancing changes have been made. #Do not expect too much content from the official release, as the Developer Team will release more updates soon to compensate for the lack of it. #An All Ages release will be announced later, as Upgradex has not met the prerequisites yet. On the 5th of July, 2026 at 20:00, Upgradex officially released to the public. === Post-Release === To incentivize playing, all valid bugs found were able to be reported for XP in the Discord server.

Developer ''TerribleAtCreating (terriac)'' noted that while the badge is present, you can't obtain it yet, as the puzzle is only partially released; What the player currently gains from the puzzle is the knowledge of knowing beforehand.

=== Update Log === Numerous minor updates were released during the time between this update and the next update, Update v1.1, mostly being bug fixes and changes.

|-| Update v1.1= Update v1.1 is the second update of Upgradex, being the third version released overall on the 1st of August, 2026 at 19:00. The update added and changed the following: :*A new Baseplate in main progression, being {{Baseplate|Ascension}} and it's respective upgrades :*Multiple new layers added across main progression and side content (being extra automation in {{Baseplate|Research}}, new upgrades in {{Baseplate|Prestige}} and a new layer in {{Baseplate|Void}} :*A portal leading to another game, [https://www.roblox.com/share?code=85e3ad193683ab49a49689abe7ff0ae4&type=ExperienceDetails&stamp=1789879037674 OPERATION: Solar Crescent] as the game's part in the collaboration between both games :*Numerous balancing changes in order to curb the advantage that players in the ''"Endgame"'' of the previous update (v1.0) had over the casual players :*Miscellaneous additions to multiple features :*[[Pyramid#Prestige Challenges|Homefinder]] has been rebalanced, leaving the old badge deprecated and archived === Pre-Release ===

On the 21st of July, 2026, ''a_sapian'' announced the update, with the following text and image:

{{Scrollbox| '''UPDATE 1.1'''

The first update for Upgradex is coming out soon! There's no hiding it now, so I'll say it: ''this update introduces the first part of the next reset layer, Ascension!'' Not only that, there will be other pretty cool Additions...

Hope to see you on 1 August 2026 at 19:00! There's a new server event for it aswell.

[[File:update1.1upcoming.png|550px|thumb|center|The attached image]] }}

On the same day, it was announced that Homefinder would be deprecated (no longer required for progression), which meant that the challenge seen in update v1.0 would be modified, and wil have it's leaderboard archived.

Then, in August 1st, 2026, a countdown message was announced around 5 hours before the update, then at 15 minutes, where the staff team hosted a live stage event in Discord as a countdown to the update.

At 19:00, August 1st, 2026, Upgradex officially had its first update. === Post-Release ===

Right as when the update released, every player received the same bug where all save files would not appear at all when joining the game. As of now, the reason is currently unspecified, and this was shortly fixed after it was discovered.

An apology was announced, detailing that the major bugs encountered during the update were most likely caused by a tighter deadline planned by the staff team themselves, leading them to having less time polishing the update. === Update Log === The following are changes and patches released after Update v1.1, but before Update v1.2:

This page details information and history about all updates and versions alike released within Upgradex, from the events leading up to it and what happened after and inbetween.
In this page, an update means a major change to the game, adding a lot of features while a change, patch or hotfix are smaller updates that help improve the game in other ways.

All individual changes are listed at the bottom of each version, and all specific times are in UTC+7 (for now).

Beta Test= From the 26th to the 28th of May 2026, Upgradex was accessible for 50 hours to players as public testing, known as the Beta Test, allowing players to have their first look at the game, albeit unfinished and unbalanced around this time. The following gameplay were included in this version: :* Main content had 3 Baseplates (specifically {{Baseplate|Main}}, {{Baseplate|Research}}, {{Baseplate|Prestige}}), with progression from upgrade {{Upgrade|Credits|#1 (New shore)}} up until the completion of [[Pyramid#Challenges|Homefinder]]. :* Optional content included 2 Baseplates (namely {{Baseplate|Bonus}} and {{Baseplate|Donation}}), wherein {{Baseplate|Bonus}} had self-inserts from the Developers and Staff Team, an extension with [[Fish Island]] relating to {{Baseplate|Bonus}} progression, and access to [[Gateway|The Gateway]], leading to {{Baseplate|Void}} which is another section of optional content. On the other hand, {{Baseplate|Donation}} was focused around Robux donations from the player, however players who couldn't donate can still progress, albeit much slower than through donating. === Pre-Release === [[File:Betaplaytestnotice.png|550px|thumb|The image posted by Lead Developer ''a_sapian'' about information relating to the Beta Test, rewards and notices]] For this period of the game, to help speed up development progress and incentivize playing, rewards were available for playing the game and reporting bugs to the developers. While not mentioned, there was also an exclusive in-game badge to those who performed a {{Data|Research Reset|symbol=no}} during the time period, known as [[Badges|BETA TESTER]].
At 13:00 May 26th, 2026, Upgradex was open to the public for the first time since development.
=== Post-Release === A few hours later, reward (b), as seen in the image contained within the section above, was then extended to be given to the top 3 best performing players instead, due to an unexpectedly high amount of CCU (Concurrent Users) seen within the game during the first hour.
With around 31 hours left during the Beta Test, Lead Developer ''a_sapian'' posted an update to current rankings relating to current points obtained through various means: [[File:Betatesthalftime.png|550px|thumb|center|Half-time statistics of the Beta Test]] Once the Beta Test concluded, a score conversion table was disclosed to the playerbase, where depending on your leaderboard placement in a currency, you would gain the respective amount of points in return, then summed up through all leaderboard catagories (except {{Data|Research Resets|symbol=no}} and {{Prestige|Prestige Resets|symbol=no}}). Then, the final statistics for the top 17 best performing players (servers) were announced: [[File:Betateststats.jpeg|550px|thumb|Final statistics posted by ''a_sapian'']] {| class="wikitable"; style="text-align:center" ! Leaderboard Placement ! In the image to the right: :*The top 3 (highlighted in '''bold''') received the Lunatic role. :*Around 21 of the top players who performed the best during this period were given the Beta Playtester+ role, instead of the normal Beta Playtester role. :* The rest of the players who had atleast 1 point were given the Beta Playtester role. However, the top player ''freakhandshake'' voluntarily gave up their Lunatic role to give to the 4th place ''mite3141'' as ''freakhandshake'' was a shared account among top players, and thus would be unethical play.

|-| Update v1.0 / Official Release= Update v1.0, also known as the official release was the first update in Upgradex, releasing alongside the game on the 5th of July, 2026. The gameplay and content featured in this version was mostly the same compared to the Beta Test version, with balancing changes and some minor additions for a smoother experience.
=== Pre-Release === 4 days before the game's release (July 1st, 2026), Lead Developer ''a_sapian'' posted an image of the number 4 with the background being taken in-game, hinting at a countdown to the initial release. Subsequent updates for the countdown were then posted when it reached 3 and 2 days, then 6 hours left respectively, with the image for the countdown being 2 days left and 6 hours left fully revealing the countdown, now reading ''"2 days left"'' and ''"6 hours left"'', extra details added with the Orthogon Studios icon in the bottom-right corner and currencies floating above. File:4countdown.png|thumb|300px|Countdown at 4 days left before release File:3countdown.png|thumb|300px|Countdown at 3 days left before release File:2countdown.png|thumb|300px|Countdown at 2 days left before release, now with extra details and the full countdown revealed File:6hourscountdown.png|thumb|300px|Countdown at 6 hours left before release, with the same details as the previous image https://youtu.be/ZaywM8mSfMo On the 4th of July, just a day before release, Developer ''TerribleAtCreating ([[Paper Dimension#terriac|terriac]])'' announced that, with the game's release, there would also be an optional badge for players to obtain, that being [[Secrets#UNREALITY|UNREALITY]], a very difficult puzzle that when solved, would reward the player the badge and the Lunatic role in the Discord server. However, this badge was to only be partially released in Update v1.0, and would only be continued with enough engagement from the community.

On the same day, Lead Developer ''a_sapian'' announced both the game's release date, being on the 5th of July, 2026 at 20:00 and uploaded Upgradex's Release Trailer, which can be watched below:

Around this time, some questions were answered relating to an All Ages release and in-game changes, which were answered below: #Data will not be carried over from the Beta Test (aka. your save files will be reset), as multiple balancing changes have been made. #Do not expect too much content from the official release, as the Developer Team will release more updates soon to compensate for the lack of it. #An All Ages release will be announced later, as Upgradex has not met the prerequisites yet. On the 5th of July, 2026 at 20:00, Upgradex officially released to the public. === Post-Release === To incentivize playing, all valid bugs found were able to be reported for XP in the Discord server.

Developer ''TerribleAtCreating (terriac)'' noted that while the badge is present, you can't obtain it yet, as the puzzle is only partially released; What the player currently gains from the puzzle is the knowledge of knowing beforehand.

|-| Update v1.1= Update v1.1 is the second update of Upgradex, being the third version released overall on the 1st of August, 2026 at 19:00. The update added and changed the following: :*A new Baseplate in main progression, being {{Baseplate|Ascension}} and it's respective upgrades :*Multiple new layers added across main progression and side content (being extra automation in {{Baseplate|Research}}, new upgrades in {{Baseplate|Prestige}} and a new layer in {{Baseplate|Void}} :*A portal leading to another game, [https://www.roblox.com/share?code=85e3ad193683ab49a49689abe7ff0ae4&type=ExperienceDetails&stamp=1789879037674 OPERATION: Solar Crescent] as the game's part in the collaboration between both games :*Numerous balancing changes in order to curb the advantage that players in the ''"Endgame"'' of the previous update (v1.0) had over the casual players :*Miscellaneous additions to multiple features :*[[Pyramid#Prestige Challenges|Homefinder]] has been rebalanced, leaving the old badge deprecated and archived === Pre-Release ===

On the 21st of July, 2026, ''a_sapian'' announced the update, with the following text and image:

{{Scrollbox| '''UPDATE 1.1'''

The first update for Upgradex is coming out soon! There's no hiding it now, so I'll say it: ''this update introduces the first part of the next reset layer, Ascension!'' Not only that, there will be other pretty cool Additions...

Hope to see you on 1 August 2026 at 19:00! There's a new server event for it aswell.

[[File:update1.1upcoming.png|550px|thumb|center|The attached image]] }}

On the same day, it was announced that Homefinder would be deprecated (no longer required for progression), which meant that the challenge seen in update v1.0 would be modified, and wil have it's leaderboard archived.

Then, in August 1st, 2026, a countdown message was announced around 5 hours before the update, then at 15 minutes, where the staff team hosted a live stage event in Discord as a countdown to the update.

At 19:00, August 1st, 2026, Upgradex officially had its first update. === Post-Release ===

Right as when the update released, every player received the same bug where all save files would not appear at all when joining the game. As of now, the reason is currently unspecified, and this was shortly fixed after it was discovered.

An apology was announced, detailing that the major bugs encountered during the update were most likely caused by a tighter deadline planned by the staff team themselves, leading them to having less time polishing the update. === Update Log === The following are changes and patches released after Update v1.1, but before Update v1.2:

This page details information and history about all updates and versions alike released within Upgradex, from the events leading up to it and what happened after and inbetween.
In this page, an update means a major change to the game, adding a lot of features while a change, patch or hotfix are smaller updates that help improve the game in other ways.

All individual changes are listed at the bottom of each version, and all specific times are in UTC+7 (for now).

Beta Test= From the 26th to the 28th of May 2026, Upgradex was accessible for 50 hours to players as public testing, known as the Beta Test, allowing players to have their first look at the game, albeit unfinished and unbalanced around this time. The following gameplay were included in this version: :* Main content had 3 Baseplates (specifically {{Baseplate|Main}}, {{Baseplate|Research}}, {{Baseplate|Prestige}}), with progression from upgrade {{Upgrade|Credits|#1 (New shore)}} up until the completion of [[Pyramid#Challenges|Homefinder]]. :* Optional content included 2 Baseplates (namely {{Baseplate|Bonus}} and {{Baseplate|Donation}}), wherein {{Baseplate|Bonus}} had self-inserts from the Developers and Staff Team, an extension with [[Fish Island]] relating to {{Baseplate|Bonus}} progression, and access to [[Gateway|The Gateway]], leading to {{Baseplate|Void}} which is another section of optional content. On the other hand, {{Baseplate|Donation}} was focused around Robux donations from the player, however players who couldn't donate can still progress, albeit much slower than through donating. === Pre-Release === [[File:Betaplaytestnotice.png|550px|thumb|The image posted by Lead Developer ''a_sapian'' about information relating to the Beta Test, rewards and notices]] For this period of the game, to help speed up development progress and incentivize playing, rewards were available for playing the game and reporting bugs to the developers. While not mentioned, there was also an exclusive in-game badge to those who performed a {{Data|Research Reset|symbol=no}} during the time period, known as [[Badges|BETA TESTER]].
At 13:00 May 26th, 2026, Upgradex was open to the public for the first time since development.
=== Post-Release === A few hours later, reward (b), as seen in the image contained within the section above, was then extended to be given to the top 3 best performing players instead, due to an unexpectedly high amount of CCU (Concurrent Users) seen within the game during the first hour.
With around 31 hours left during the Beta Test, Lead Developer ''a_sapian'' posted an update to current rankings relating to current points obtained through various means: [[File:Betatesthalftime.png|550px|thumb|center|Half-time statistics of the Beta Test]] Once the Beta Test concluded, a score conversion table was disclosed to the playerbase, where depending on your leaderboard placement in a currency, you would gain the respective amount of points in return, then summed up through all leaderboard catagories (except {{Data|Research Resets|symbol=no}} and {{Prestige|Prestige Resets|symbol=no}}). Then, the final statistics for the top 17 best performing players (servers) were announced: [[File:Betateststats.jpeg|550px|thumb|Final statistics posted by ''a_sapian'']] {| class="wikitable"; style="text-align:center" ! Leaderboard Placement ! Points Gained |- | 1st Place | +100pts |- | 2nd Place | +60pts |- | 3rd Place | +40pts |- | 4th Place | +25pts |- | 5th Place | +18pts |- | 6th Place | +14pts |- | 7th Place | +11pts |- | 8th Place | +8pts |- | 9th Place | +6pts |- | 10th Place | +5pts |}
In the image to the right: :*The top 3 (highlighted in '''bold''') received the Lunatic role. :*Around 21 of the top players who performed the best during this period were given the Beta Playtester+ role, instead of the normal Beta Playtester role. :* The rest of the players who had atleast 1 point were given the Beta Playtester role. However, the top player ''freakhandshake'' voluntarily gave up their Lunatic role to give to the 4th place ''mite3141'' as ''freakhandshake'' was a shared account among top players, and thus would be unethical play.

|-| Update v1.0 / Official Release= Update v1.0, also known as the official release was the first update in Upgradex, releasing alongside the game on the 5th of July, 2026. The gameplay and content featured in this version was mostly the same compared to the Beta Test version, with balancing changes and some minor additions for a smoother experience.
=== Pre-Release === 4 days before the game's release (July 1st, 2026), Lead Developer ''a_sapian'' posted an image of the number 4 with the background being taken in-game, hinting at a countdown to the initial release. Subsequent updates for the countdown were then posted when it reached 3 and 2 days, then 6 hours left respectively, with the image for the countdown being 2 days left and 6 hours left fully revealing the countdown, now reading ''"2 days left"'' and ''"6 hours left"'', extra details added with the Orthogon Studios icon in the bottom-right corner and currencies floating above. File:4countdown.png|thumb|300px|Countdown at 4 days left before release File:3countdown.png|thumb|300px|Countdown at 3 days left before release File:2countdown.png|thumb|300px|Countdown at 2 days left before release, now with extra details and the full countdown revealed File:6hourscountdown.png|thumb|300px|Countdown at 6 hours left before release, with the same details as the previous image https://youtu.be/ZaywM8mSfMo On the 4th of July, just a day before release, Developer ''TerribleAtCreating ([[Paper Dimension#terriac|terriac]])'' announced that, with the game's release, there would also be an optional badge for players to obtain, that being [[Secrets#UNREALITY|UNREALITY]], a very difficult puzzle that when solved, would reward the player the badge and the Lunatic role in the Discord server. However, this badge was to only be partially released in Update v1.0, and would only be continued with enough engagement from the community.

Developer ''TerribleAtCreating (terriac)'' noted that while the badge is present, you can't obtain it yet, as the puzzle is only partially released; What the player currently gains from the puzzle is the knowledge of knowing beforehand.

On the same day, Lead Developer ''a_sapian'' announced both the game's release date, being on the 5th of July, 2026 at 20:00 and uploaded Upgradex's Release Trailer, which can be watched below:

Around this time, some questions were answered relating to an All Ages release and in-game changes, which were answered below: #Data will not be carried over from the Beta Test (aka. your save files will be reset), as multiple balancing changes have been made. #Do not expect too much content from the official release, as the Developer Team will release more updates soon to compensate for the lack of it. #An All Ages release will be announced later, as Upgradex has not met the prerequisites yet. On the 5th of July, 2026 at 20:00, Upgradex officially released to the public. === Post-Release === To incentivize playing, all valid bugs found were able to be reported for XP in the Discord server. === Update Log === Numerous minor updates were released during the time between this update and the next update, Update v1.1, mostly being bug fixes and changes.

|-| Update v1.1= Update v1.1 is the second update of Upgradex, being the third version released overall on the 1st of August, 2026 at 19:00. The update added and changed the following: :*A new Baseplate in main progression, being {{Baseplate|Ascension}} and it's respective upgrades :*Multiple new layers added across main progression and side content (being extra automation in {{Baseplate|Research}}, new upgrades in {{Baseplate|Prestige}} and a new layer in {{Baseplate|Void}} :*A portal leading to another game, [https://www.roblox.com/share?code=85e3ad193683ab49a49689abe7ff0ae4&type=ExperienceDetails&stamp=1789879037674 OPERATION: Solar Crescent] as the game's part in the collaboration between both games :*Numerous balancing changes in order to curb the advantage that players in the ''"Endgame"'' of the previous update (v1.0) had over the casual players :*Miscellaneous additions to multiple features :*[[Pyramid#Prestige Challenges|Homefinder]] has been rebalanced, leaving the old badge deprecated and archived === Pre-Release ===

On the 21st of July, 2026, ''a_sapian'' announced the update, with the following text and image:

{{Scrollbox| '''UPDATE 1.1'''

The first update for Upgradex is coming out soon! There's no hiding it now, so I'll say it: ''this update introduces the first part of the next reset layer, Ascension!'' Not only that, there will be other pretty cool Additions...

Hope to see you on 1 August 2026 at 19:00! There's a new server event for it aswell.

[[File:update1.1upcoming.png|550px|thumb|center|The attached image]] }}

On the same day, it was announced that Homefinder would be deprecated (no longer required for progression), which meant that the challenge seen in update v1.0 would be modified, and wil have it's leaderboard archived.

Then, in August 1st, 2026, a countdown message was announced around 5 hours before the update, then at 15 minutes, where the staff team hosted a live stage event in Discord as a countdown to the update.

At 19:00, August 1st, 2026, Upgradex officially had its first update. === Post-Release ===

Right as when the update released, every player received the same bug where all save files would not appear at all when joining the game. As of now, the reason is currently unspecified, and this was shortly fixed after it was discovered.

An apology was announced, detailing that the major bugs encountered during the update were most likely caused by a tighter deadline planned by the staff team themselves, leading them to having less time polishing the update. === Update Log === The following are changes and patches released after Update v1.1, but before Update v1.2:

This page details information and history about all updates and versions alike released within Upgradex, from the events leading up to it and what happened after and inbetween.
In this page, an update means a major change to the game, adding a lot of features while a change, patch or hotfix are smaller updates that help improve the game in other ways. All individual changes are listed at the bottom of each version, and all specific times are in UTC+7 {{Color|Grey|(for now)}}. Beta Test= From the 26th to the 28th of May 2026, Upgradex was accessible for 50 hours to players as public testing, known as the Beta Test, allowing players to have their first look at the game, albeit unfinished and unbalanced around this time. The following gameplay were included in this version: :* Main content had 3 Baseplates (specifically {{Baseplate|Main}}, {{Baseplate|Research}}, {{Baseplate|Prestige}}), with progression from upgrade {{Upgrade|Credits|#1 (New shore)}} up until the completion of {{Challenge|Homefinder}}. :* Optional content included 2 Baseplates (namely {{Baseplate|Bonus}} and {{Baseplate|Donation}}), wherein {{Baseplate|Bonus}} had self-inserts from the Developers and Staff Team, an extension with {{Baseplate|Fish}} relating to {{Baseplate|Bonus}} progression, and access to [[Gateway|The Gateway]], leading to {{Baseplate|Void}} which is another section of optional content. On the other hand, {{Baseplate|Donation}} was focused around Robux donations from the player, however players who couldn't donate can still progress, albeit much slower than through donating. === Pre-Release === [[File:Betaplaytestnotice.png|550px|thumb|The image posted by Lead Developer ''a_sapian'' about information relating to the Beta Test, rewards and notices]] For this period of the game, to help speed up development progress and incentivize playing, rewards were available for playing the game and reporting bugs to the developers. While not mentioned, there was also an exclusive in-game badge to those who performed a {{Data|Research Reset|symbol=no}} during the time period, known as [[Badges|BETA TESTER]]. At 13:00 May 26th, 2026, Upgradex was open to the public for the first time since development.
=== Post-Release === A few hours later, reward (b), as seen in the image contained within the section above, was then extended to be given to the top 3 best performing players instead, due to an unexpectedly high amount of CCU {{Color|Grey|(Concurrent Users)}} seen within the game during the first hour.
With around 31 hours left during the Beta Test, Lead Developer ''a_sapian'' posted an update to current rankings relating to current points obtained through various leaderboards: [[File:Betatesthalftime.png|550px|thumb|center|Half-time statistics of the Beta Test]] Once the Beta Test concluded, a score conversion table was disclosed to the playerbase, where depending on your leaderboard placement in a statistic, you would gain the respective amount of points in return, then summed up through all 6 included leaderboard catagories (not including {{Data|Research Resets|symbol=no}} and {{Prestige|Prestige Resets|symbol=no}}). Then, the final statistics for the top 17 best performing players (servers) were announced: [[File:Betateststats.jpeg|550px|thumb|Final statistics posted by ''a_sapian'']] {| class="wikitable"; style="text-align:center" ! Leaderboard Placement ! Points Gained |- | 1st Place | +100pts |- | 2nd Place | +60pts |- | 3rd Place | +40pts |- | 4th Place | +25pts |- | 5th Place | +18pts |- | 6th Place | +14pts |- | 7th Place | +11pts |- | 8th Place | +8pts |- | 9th Place | +6pts |- | 10th Place | +5pts |}
In the image to the right: :*The top 3 (highlighted in '''bold''') received the Lunatic role. :*The rest of the players who had at least 1 point were given the Beta Playtester+ role {{Color|Grey|(21 total, 4 were not included)}} instead of the normal Beta Playtester role. However, the top player ''freakhandshake'' voluntarily gave up their Lunatic role to give to the 4th place ''mite3141'' as ''freakhandshake'' was a shared account among top players, and thus would be unethical play.

|-| Update v1.0 / Official Release= Update v1.0, also known as the official release was the first update in Upgradex, releasing alongside the game on the 5th of July, 2026. The gameplay and content featured in this version was mostly the same compared to the Beta Test version, with balancing changes and some minor additions for a smoother experience.
=== Pre-Release === 4 days before the game's release (July 1st, 2026), Lead Developer ''a_sapian'' posted an image of the number 4 with the background being taken in-game, hinting at a countdown to the initial release. Subsequent updates for the countdown were then posted when it reached 3 and 2 days, then 6 hours left respectively. With the image for the 2-day and 6-hour countdowns fully revealing the countdown, now reading ''"2 days left"'' and ''"6 hours left"'', extra details were added including the Orthogon Studios icon in the bottom-right corner and currencies floating above. File:4countdown.png|thumb|300px|Countdown at 4 days left before release File:3countdown.png|thumb|300px|Countdown at 3 days left before release File:2countdown.png|thumb|300px|Countdown at 2 days left before release, now with extra details and the full countdown revealed File:6hourscountdown.png|thumb|300px|Countdown at 6 hours left before release, with the same details as the previous image https://youtu.be/ZaywM8mSfMo On the 4th of July, just a day before release, Developer ''TerribleAtCreating ([[Paper Dimension#terriac|terriac]])'' announced that, with the game's release, there would also be an optional badge for players to obtain, that being [[Secrets#UNREALITY|UNREALITY]], a very difficult puzzle that, when solved, would reward the player the badge and the Lunatic role in the Discord server. However, this badge was to only be partially released in Update v1.0, and would only be continued with enough engagement from the community.

Developer ''TerribleAtCreating (terriac)'' noted that while the badge is present, you can't obtain it yet, as the puzzle is only partially released; What the player currently gains from the puzzle is the knowledge of knowing beforehand.

On the same day, Lead Developer ''a_sapian'' announced both the game's release date, being on the 5th of July, 2026 at 20:00 and uploaded Upgradex's Release Trailer, which can be watched above:

Around this time, some questions were answered relating to an All Ages release and in-game changes, which were answered below: #Data will not be carried over from the Beta Test (aka. players' save files from before release will be reset), as multiple balancing changes have been made. #Do not expect too much content from the official release, as the Upgradex Team will release more updates soon to compensate for the lack of it. #An All Ages release will be announced later, as Upgradex has not met the prerequisites yet. On the 5th of July, 2026 at 20:00, Upgradex officially released to the public. === Post-Release === To incentivize playing, all valid bugs found were able to be reported for XP in the Discord server. === Update Log === Numerous minor updates were released during the time between this update and the next update, Update v1.1, mostly being bug fixes and changes.

|-| Update v1.1= Update v1.1 is the second update of Upgradex, being the third version released overall on the 1st of August, 2026 at 19:00. The update added and changed the following: :*A new Baseplate in main progression, being {{Baseplate|Ascension}} and it's respective upgrades :*Multiple new layers added across main progression and side content (being extra automation in {{Baseplate|Research}}, new upgrades in {{Baseplate|Prestige}} and a new layer in {{Baseplate|Void}} :*A portal leading to another game, [https://www.roblox.com/share?code=85e3ad193683ab49a49689abe7ff0ae4&type=ExperienceDetails&stamp=1789879037674 OPERATION: Solar Crescent] as the game's part in the collaboration between both games :*Numerous balancing changes in order to curb the advantage that players in the ''"Endgame"'' of the previous update (v1.0) had over the casual players :*Miscellaneous additions to multiple features :*{{Challenge|Homefinder}} has been rebalanced, leaving the old badge deprecated and archived === Pre-Release ===

On the 21st of July, 2026, ''a_sapian'' announced the update, with the following text and image:

{{Scrollbox| '''UPDATE 1.1'''

The first update for Upgradex is coming out soon! There's no hiding it now, so I'll say it: ''this update introduces the first part of the next reset layer, Ascension!'' Not only that, there will be other pretty cool Additions...

Hope to see you on 1 August 2026 at 19:00! There's a new server event for it aswell.

[[File:update1.1upcoming.png|550px|thumb|center|The attached image]] }}

On the same day, it was announced that {{Challenge|Homefinder}} would be deprecated (no longer required for progression), which meant that the challenge seen in update v1.0 would be modified, and wil have it's leaderboard archived.

Then, in August 1st, 2026, a countdown message was announced around 5 hours before the update, then at 15 minutes, where the staff team hosted a live stage event in Discord as a countdown to the update.

At 19:00, August 1st, 2026, Upgradex officially had its first major update. === Post-Release ===

Right as when the update released, every player received the same bug where all save files would not appear at all when joining the game. As of now, the reason is currently unspecified, and this was shortly fixed after it was discovered.

An apology was announced, detailing that the major bugs encountered during the update were most likely caused by a tighter deadline planned by the staff team themselves, leading them to having less time polishing the update. === Update Log === The following are changes and patches released after Update v1.1, but before Update v1.2:

{{Stub|General info, characters and dialogue}}
The '''Paper Dimension''', commonly known as terriac's Pocket Dimension, is a [[location]] hidden within the [[Bonus Baseplate]]. As the name might suggest, it is a landscape themed around the Fundamental Paper Education universe. Its main purpose is to host terriac's house, along with some of the staff team's original characters, and is also the starting point for the [[Badges|UNREALITY]] badge.
== Features ==
=== Cube Teleporter ===
[[File:CubeTeleporter.png|200px|thumb|right]] :''Main article: [[Cube Telepoter]]'' The {{Credits|Cube teleporter|symbol=no}} is a feature unlocked by multiple upgrades. It allows the player to teleport to different zones of the game.
=== Flying notes ===
=== Seesaw ===
[[File:Seesaw.png|200px|thumb|right]] The Seesaw is a basic feature of terriac's house. This seesaw is interactive, you can sit on it to tip it towards either side.
=== Tire Swing ===
[[File:Tire_Swing.png|200px|thumb|right]] The Tire Swing is a basic feature of terriac's house. This tire swing can be sat on, which allows you to swing around in it.
=== Slide ===
[[File:Slide.png|200px|thumb|right]] :''Main article: [[Slide]]'' The Slide is a basic feature of terriac's house. At the top of this slide is a trip part that allows you to slide down and plummet into the lake.
== Characters == === terriac ===
[[File:Terriac.png|200px|thumb|right]] :''Main article: [[terriac]]'' terriac is the owner of the Paper Dimension and his house. He answers questions related to the Paper Dimension and also holds one dialogue choice hinting at the UNREALITY badge. He is seen pondering while lying against his bed.
=== Connor ===
<!-->Don't make a main article for him until you see him again<--> Connor is a neutral character that resides outside of terriac's house. He is a personified metal sign that accessorizes with a long orange and black striped scarf, whose design resembles caution tape. He does not currently have any dialogue. Connor initially appears camouflaged as a warning sign. The only interaction the player can have with Connor is to approach him, at which point he will reveal his face and start looking at the player. Walking away from Connor will cause him to revert to his camouflaged state. As seen in a dialogue choice for terriac, there are other unknown characters associated with Connor.
=== Arayde ===
[[File:Arayde.png|200px|thumb|right]] :''Main article: [[Arayde]]'' Arayde is an original character made by Raspbelvet. He occupies the school-like space in Terriac's house. According to terriac, the reasoning for this is that someone rented out the lower floor of his house to make a school out of it. (Needs info.)
=== Stellaria ===
[[File:Stellaria.png|200px|thumb|right]] :''Main article: [[Stellaria]]'' Stellaria is an original character made by Sandie. She accessorises with a leotard. (Definitely needs info.) <!-->I found a few notes relating to Stellaria but I have no idea how to interpret them. Please contact me for them<-->
